# Mātugāma Saṁyutta (SN 37)

**ID:** SN 37  
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Mātugāma Saṁyutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul2.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul2.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mātugāma Saṁyutta* (SN 37) is the thirty-seventh collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, comprising thirty-four short discourses centering on women [Bodhi 2003a]. The collection addresses topics such as the physical and moral factors that make a woman agreeable or disagreeable to a man (including beauty, wealth, ethical conduct, industriousness, and bearing children), as well as corresponding factors that attract women to men [Bodhi 2003a; Bodhi 2003b; Cabezón 2017; Hazra 1994]. It details the kinds of suffering unique to women (*āveṇikāni dukkhāni*) that are not experienced by men, qualities like wide learning that benefit women, and the moral causes leading to rebirth in fortunate or unfortunate realms [Freedman 1977; Bodhi 2003a; Bodhi 2003c]. The Venerable Anuruddha features prominently as an interlocutor in many of these suttas, inquiring about women's rebirths by means of his development of the divine eye (*dibbacakkhu*) [Bodhi 2003a; Bodhi 2003c]. Textual arrangements vary slightly among recensions: Burmese (*Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana*) and Siamese editions present suttas 5–24 as addressed to Anuruddha, whereas the Pali Text Society edition organizes the opening formulas differently [Bodhi 2003c].

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 2003a] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A Translation of the Saṁyutta Nikāya (2000/2003), Introduction to SN 37 — Overview of sutta count, major themes, and Anuruddha's role.
- [Bodhi 2003b] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A Translation of the Saṁyutta Nikāya (2000/2003), text of SN 37 — Five factors that make a woman agreeable or disagreeable to a man.
- [Bodhi 2003c] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A Translation of the Saṁyutta Nikāya (2000/2003), notes to SN 37 — Textual variations between PTS, Burmese, and Siamese editions, and commentary on unique suffering.
- [Cabezón 2017] José Ignacio Cabezón, Sexuality in Classical South Asian Buddhism (2017) — Discussion of the five attractive qualities applied to both women and men.
- [Freedman 1977] Michael Freedman, The Characterization of Ānanda in the Pāli Canon of the Theravāda (1977) — Note on wide learning as one of the qualities mentioned in the samyutta.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Summary of the five qualities that charm a man.
